<!-- thmx-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:maintheorem}
Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete $C^*$-simple group and let $\mu$ be
an invariant random subgroup of $\Gamma$. Then $H$ is $C^*$-simple for
$\mu$-almost every $H\in\operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)$.
<!-- end thmx-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:freebndry}
Let $Y$ be a free $\Gamma$-boundary. There exists a free compact
metrizable boundary as a factor of $Y$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For each $s\ne e$, the open
sets $\{y\in Y:f(y)\ne f(sy)\}$, with $f\in C(Y)$, cover $Y$.
By compactness, choose a finite family $F_s\subseteq C(Y)$ giving
such a cover. Let $A\subseteq C(Y)$ be the unital $C^*$-algebra
generated by all $\Gamma$-translates of the functions in
$\bigcup_{s\ne e}F_s$. Since $\Gamma$ is countable, $A$ is separable.
Its spectrum $X$ is compact metrizable, and the inclusion
$A\subseteq C(Y)$ induces a continuous equivariant surjection
$p:Y\to X$. If $sx=x$ for some $s\ne e$, choose $y\in p^{-1}(x)$.
Then $p(sy)=p(y)$, so $f(sy)=f(y)$ for every $f\in A$, contradicting
the choice of $F_s$. Thus the action on $X$ is free. Finally, since boundary actions pass to factors, we see that $X$ is a $\Gamma$-boundary.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:convmeasurable}
Let $X$ be a compact metric space. Then, the map $${\rm Conv}:\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))\setminus\{\varnothing\} \to \mathcal{CC}(\operatorname{Prob}(X)), ~A\mapsto \overline{{\rm Conv}}^{w^*}(A)$$
is continuous. If $X$ is a $\Gamma$-space, then the map ${\rm Conv}$ is moreover $\Gamma$-equivariant.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Indeed, since every continuous affine function takes its extreme values on extreme points, for every
$A\in\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ and $f\in C(X,\mathbb{R})$, $$h_f\bigl(\overline{\operatorname{Conv}}^{\,w^*}A\bigr)
 =\max_{\nu\in A}\nu(f).$$
It is straightforward to see that the map $A\mapsto \max_{\nu\in A}\nu(f)$ is continuous on $\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ for every $f\in C(X,\mathbb{R})$. This implies the continuity of the map ${\rm Conv}:\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))\setminus\{\varnothing\} \to \mathcal{CC}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))$.
The last assertion about equivariance is straightforward.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:union-measurable}
Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete group and let $X$ be a compact
metrizable $\Gamma$-space. The map
$Q:\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma))\xrightarrow[]{}\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))$ defined by $Q(E)=\operatorname{Prob}_E(X)$
is $\Gamma$-equivariant and Borel measurable.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
For $H\le \Gamma$, we have $\operatorname{Prob}_{gHg^{-1}}(X)=\{g\nu: \nu\in \operatorname{Prob}_{H}(X)\}$, which in turn implies that $Q$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant.
To see it is Borel measurable, as remarked in the previous section, it is enough to show that the set $\{E\in \mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma)):Q(E)\cap D\ne\varnothing\}$
is closed for every closed set  $D\subseteq\operatorname{Prob}(X)$. For this,
let $E_n\to E$ in $\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma))$, and let $H_n\in E_n$ and $\nu_n\in D\cap\operatorname{Prob}_{H_n}(X)$. By passing to a subsequence, we may assume $H_n\to H\in E$ and $\nu_n\to\nu\in D$. This gives $\nu\in\operatorname{Prob}_H(X)$, and the claim follows.
Hence, $Q$ is Borel measurable.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:ordered-selection}
Let $Y$ be a compact metrizable space equipped with a closed preorder
{$\preccurlyeq$}.
The maps $\operatorname{Min}(\cdot, \preccurlyeq)$ and $\operatorname{Max}(\cdot, \preccurlyeq)$ on $\mathcal{K}(Y)$ are Borel.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $C\in \mathcal{K}(Y)$, and let $(A_n)$ be a sequence in $\mathcal{K}(Y)$ such that $\operatorname{Min}(A_n, \preccurlyeq) \cap C\ne \varnothing$ and $A_n\to A\in \mathcal{K}(Y)$. Choose a sequence $y_n\in \operatorname{Min}(A_n, \preccurlyeq) \cap C$, and by passing to a subsequence, assume $y_n\to y\in Y$. Since $C$ is closed, $y\in C$, and since $A_n\to A$, we have $y\in A$. Let $a\in A$. Then there exists $a_n\in A_n$ such that $a_n\to a$. Since $y_n \preccurlyeq a_n$, closedness of $\preccurlyeq$ implies $y\preccurlyeq a$. Thus, $y\in \operatorname{Min}(A, \preccurlyeq) \cap C$. This implies that the map $A\mapsto \operatorname{Min}(A, \preccurlyeq)$ on $\mathcal{K}(Y)$ is Borel measurable. Considering  $\preccurlyeq^{op}$, we also conclude that the map $A\mapsto \operatorname{Max}(A, \preccurlyeq)$ is Borel.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:Ami}
The map ${\rm Ami}: \operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)\to \mathcal{K}(\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma)))$ defined by $H\mapsto \mathcal{K}^H(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(H))$ is Borel.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $C\in\mathcal{K}(\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma)))$, and let
$H_n\to H$ in $\operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)$ such that
$\mathcal{K}^{H_n}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(H_n))\cap C\ne\varnothing$.
Choose $E_n\in\mathcal{K}^{H_n}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(H_n))\cap C$.
By passing to a subsequence, assume $E_n\to E\in C$. Let $L\in E$, and choose $L_n\in E_n$ such that $L_n\to L$.
Since $L_n\le H_n$, we have $L\le H$. Thus
$E\subseteq\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(H)$.
Moreover, for $h\in H$, we have $h\in H_n$ eventually, so
$hE_nh^{-1}=E_n$ eventually, and hence $hEh^{-1}=E$.
Since the empty set is isolated in the hyperspace, $E$ is nonempty.
Therefore, $E\in\mathcal{K}^H(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(H))\cap C$ and the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:AH-borel}
For every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the map
$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{URS}}:\operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)\to
\mathcal{K}(\operatorname{Sub}^{\mathrm{am}}(\Gamma))$, defined by
$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{URS}}(H)=\mathcal{A}_H$, is $\Gamma$-equivariant and Borel measurable.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
We have
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{URS}}(\cdot) = \operatorname{Min}\Big(\operatorname{Max}\big({\rm Ami}(\cdot),\sqsubseteq\big), \subseteq\Big)
\]
and therefore it is Borel by Lemma~\ref{lem:ordered-selection} and Lemma~\ref{lem:Ami}.

The equivariance of the map follows from the fact that $g\mathcal{A}_Hg^{-1}=\mathcal{A}_{gHg^{-1}}$ for every $g\in \Gamma$ and $H\le \Gamma$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete $C^*$-simple group and let $\mu$
be an IRS of $\Gamma$. Its action on $\partial_F\Gamma$ is free
by \cite{KK}. Using Lemma~\ref{lem:freebndry}, we obtain a free compact
metrizable $\Gamma$-boundary $X$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:convmeasurable}, Lemma~\ref{lem:union-measurable}, and Proposition~\ref{prop:AH-borel}, the map $\Phi = {\rm Conv}\circ Q \circ \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{URS}}: \operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)\to \mathcal{CC}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant and Borel measurable.
Consequently, $\Phi_*\mu$ is a $\Gamma$-invariant Borel
probability measure on $\mathcal{CC}(\operatorname{Prob}(X))$. Since $X$ is a boundary,
$\operatorname{Prob}(X)$ is an irreducible affine $\Gamma$-space. Hence it follows from
\cite[Lemma~2.3]{BDL} that $\Phi_*\mu=\delta_{\operatorname{Prob}(X)}$.
Therefore, there is a measurable $\mu$-conull set $\Omega\subseteq\operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)$ such that $\overline{\operatorname{Conv}}^{\,w^*}\operatorname{Prob}_{\mathcal{A}_H}(X)=\operatorname{Prob}(X)$ for every $H\in\Omega$.
Fix $H\in\Omega$ and $x\in X$.
By Milman's converse to the Krein--Milman theorem, $\delta_x\in\operatorname{Prob}_{\mathcal{A}_H}(X)$.
But since the action of $\Gamma$ on $X$ is free, it follows that $\{e\}\in\mathcal{A}_H$, and so $\mathcal{A}_H=\{\{e\}\}$.
Hence, $H$ is $C^*$-simple for $\mu$-almost every $H\in \operatorname{Sub}(\Gamma)$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
